newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee stays firm on selling of dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee stays firm on selling of dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed firm due to continuous selling of dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.69, after opening at its previous closing level of 56.70, they said.
"The rupee gained on early selling of dollars by a foreign name, and stayed firm as banks generated the local currency when call rates rose slightly," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
Overnight call rates went to 14.5 percent after opening at 13.75, dealers said.
"Even this marginal rise in call money saw banks generating rupees, because dollar rupee trade was dull, and banks had excess dollars," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
A dull forex market saw banks opt for a high yielding currency, which served to keep the dollar down locally despite the U.S. unit's overseas strength, he said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 1.5 local cents in line with its overseas movement, and set buying and selling prices at 56.0909 and 57.2241.
